title: Frozen Tissue Nuclei Extraction Protocol
author: Carly Martin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7xchpiw
materials: Make dissociation buffer , 50 mLs per sample:

Prepare equipment: Set out and chill the following equipment/supplies. The instructions below are for one sample. ● Cold block dissecting tray, kept at -20C ● Chill clean razor blades and glass slides on the cold dissecting tray ● Chill 3 mL syringe with 26 1⁄2 gauge needle, at 4C, one syringe and needle per sample ● Place a 12-well tissue-culture plate, well-bottoms colored with marker, on ice * Color the underside of the culture plate with dark marker so you can see your sample dissociate ● Place 2 mL chilled extraction buffer in the first well of 12-well plate ● Place ~50 mL chilled DB in a falcon tube on ice ● Locate DAPI (1:1000) (https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/D1306) ● Locate 50 μm eppendorf tube filter, place in 4C (https://us.sysmex-flowcytometry.com/consumables/celltrics-filters/sterile-single-p ack-celltrics filters/1445/sterile-single-pack-celltrics-filters-50/box?number=04-00 4-2327) ● Place 2 50 mL tubes on ice ● Locate a c-Chip FR hemocytometer
Chill all buffers to 4C , and keep all buffers on ice when in use.

Begin extraction. Perform all steps with cold buffers on ice. Nuclei should never leave the ice or 4C environment. Chop up tissue on the chilled dissection tray. If your sample is a very small piece (less than 3mm in any dimension) you can forgo this step and place sample immediately into the extraction buffer Place the frozen sample on the glass slide and shave the frosty/freezer-burned tissue face you want to sample from off the sample and discard. This is damaged and not worth extracting. Then, moving rapidly but carefully, shave off “enough” sample to work with. Rapidly mince the shaved sample with the 2 chilled razor blades that were used to shave the tissue block and scrape into the first well of a 6-well plate that contains 2 mL of cold extraction buffer. Pipette up and down 20 times.

Locate supplies for FACS: ● 96 well cold block, chilled to -20C: (https://www.daigger.com/eppendorf-pcr-coolers-14616-group?gclid=EAIaIQobCh MI2rKM7aDN4AIVDRgMCh2jkwRMEAQYBSABEgKeA_D_BwE) ● 200uL 5% BSA-DB ● 20uL collection buffer: DB with 1:40 RNAse-inhibitor * Prepare the collection buffer right before beginning FACS session

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffer
steps.instruction: For each sample, prepare 3 mL extraction buffer by mixing Dissociation Buffer with 1 % (v/v) Kollidon VA64, 1 % (v/v) Triton X100, and RNase‑inhibitor at a 1:40 ratio.

steps.title: Incubate with detergent and trituration
steps.instruction: Incubate the sample in the extraction buffer for 10 min while pipetting up and down 20 times, approximately every 2.5 min, using a 1000 µL pipette set to 1000 µL.

steps.title: Mechanical dissociation with syringe
steps.instruction: Pull the sample into a chilled needle/syringe and expel it back into the same well for a final mechanical dissociation; repeat the pull‑and‑express cycle if visible large chunks remain.

steps.title: Large volume wash of nuclei
steps.instruction: Transfer the nuclei into an empty 30 mL tube and add chilled DB until the total volume is just under 30 mL.

steps.title: Divide nuclei into conical tubes
steps.instruction: Aliquot the diluted nuclei into two 50 mL conical tubes, aiming for ~15 mL per tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge nuclei at 600 rcf
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 600 rcf in a swinging‑bucket rotor for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Aspirate supernatant and resuspend nuclei
steps.instruction: Aspirate supernatant, leave a small volume, and resuspend nuclei without introducing bubbles, then pool the appropriate tube pairs.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate ~13 mL wash buffer with a serological pipette.
Gently aspirate the remaining supernatant with a P1000 pipette, leaving 300–500 µL of liquid.
Resuspend the nuclei by pipetting gently, avoiding bubbles.
Pool the corresponding tube pairs back together.

steps.title: Filter nuclei through 40 µm filter
steps.instruction: Wet a 40 µm Eppendorf filter tip with cold DB, then pass 0.5–1 mL of the washed nuclei suspension through the filter into an Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Stain nuclei with DAPI
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL DAPI to 1 mL of nuclei suspension, mix, then remove 20 µL and load into a Fast‑Read hemocytometer to assess concentration and quality.

steps.title: FACS enrichment of singlet nuclei
steps.instruction: Using a Sony SH800 sorter with a 70 µm chip, gate on the singlet DAPI peak (1 % FSC threshold) and collect sorted nuclei into PCR tubes placed on a chilled (‑20 °C) 96‑well block.

steps.title: Prepare PCR collection tubes
steps.instruction: Coat, wash, and add collection buffer to PCR tubes before FACS collection.

substeps.instruction: Fill the PCR tube with 5 % BSA‑DB, vortex, and discard the BSA solution to coat the tube walls.
Wash the tube with 200 µL DB.
Add 20 µL collection buffer (DB containing RNase‑inhibitor at 1:40) to the tube.
Collect sorted nuclei into the prepared tube as described in the previous step.

steps.title: Determine nuclei concentration
steps.instruction: Make a 1:10 dilution of the sorted nuclei, count with a hemocytometer, and calculate the final concentration in nuclei/µL.

substeps.instruction: Measure the volume in each PCR tube.
Combine 2 µL nuclei with 18 µL chilled DB to create a 1:10 dilution.
Load the dilution into a Fast‑Read hemocytometer and image all 16 large squares.
Count nuclei in each square, compute the average, multiply by 10 (dilution factor) and then by 5 (hemocytometer factor) to obtain nuclei per µL.

steps.title: Prepare nuclei for 10X sequencing
steps.instruction: For 10× Genomics v3, limit input to 17 000 nuclei (≈10 000 after loss), which corresponds to 46.6 µL at a maximum concentration of 364 nuclei/µL.
